summary:
As I’m sure you’ve heard by now, we have a little new baby named Christo­ pher. So all we do is baby stuff, which I won’t bore you with. We put in a phone for you to call us, and so wrote you, but you never did or else if you did we weren’t home or refused to answer or you pretended to be someone else and I never guessed. Who did you pretend to be? Linda Levy, my ex-girlfriend? But she never phoned either. So maybe you pretended to be Linda Levy pretending to be 
Dr. Willis McNelly of Cal State Fullerton, who did call. But anyhow there is no use calling now because Christopher will answer and simulate an idiot, wasting your money if not time. 

Try it, though; it costs one dollar to phone late at night anywhere in Califor­ nia. Think of it this way: it will save you having to write. And I will refund your dollar (not right away, maybe, but eventually). (And you know what that means.) One reason for my writing you is I’ve lost Bob Silverberg’s address because we moved to another apartment and lost a lot of things like the cat, the goat, all my books, the stereo, etc. (I exaggerate.) Norman Spinrad was down here the other day and mentioned that Bob is doing a bibliography or sumpin’ for H.E.W. on s-f stories and novels dealing with dope. That woke me up. What I want to let Bob know (if this be true) is that I have a new novel, FLOW MY TEARS, THE POLICEMAN SAID coming out in Feb of next year by Double­ day, and it is very anti-dope.
